Maintenance Report — MNT-0188-001

Asset: WELL-0188 (NE-08 Well 188, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 02 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 14 Dec 2022 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 280 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0188-0007 on 2022-12-01 Report written: 15 Dec 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0188-0007 showed the wellhead at 16.8 °C with the air at 11.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 10 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD

Rig services3,986
Consumables1,594
Labour (company crew and contractor)8,849
Total24,793

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 4 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0188-007

Asset: WELL-0188 (NE-08 Well 188, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 10 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Nov 2023 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 289 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0188-0054 on 2023-11-09 Report written: 23 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0188-0054 showed the wellhead at 18.4 °C with the air at 18.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0188-013

Asset: WELL-0188 (NE-08 Well 188, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 07 May 2024 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 95 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0188-0079 on 2024-05-02 Report written: 08 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0188-0079 showed the wellhead at 32.9 °C with the air at 27.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0188-016

Asset: WELL-0188 (NE-08 Well 188, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 18 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 29 Oct 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 266 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0188-0101 on 2024-10-17 Report written: 29 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0188-0101 showed the wellhead at 22.7 °C with the air at 18.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,444
Bolts, shims and seals361
Bearing grease and consumables602
Labour (company crew and contractor)1,627
Total4,034

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten the same day as the work (limit 3 days)
Manual §10Action required3 corrective repairs on this equipment in 12 months; root-cause analysis to be started

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0188-026

Asset: WELL-0188 (NE-08 Well 188, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 12 Dec 2025 08:00 · Finished: 12 Dec 2025 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 11 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0188-0161 on 2025-12-11 Report written: 14 Dec 2025

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0188-0161 at 12:45 on 2025-12-11 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.7% of the pad area, estimated 0.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 208 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 166 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0188-026 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.33% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Line pipe and fittings2,115
Absorbents and berms940
Soil hauling and disposal1,645
Labour (company crew and contractor)4,319
Total9,019

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-04MetPermit issued; gas test 0% LEL
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)
SR-02MetContained about 2.1 hours after discovery (limit 4 hours)
SR-04MetSpill recorded with volume and area (minor class)
SR-03MetCleaned to below 1.0% TPH; agency verification applies only to reportable spills

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
